o1.biggest_strength: Locks onto the winning segment, the pricing-change trigger and the no-link step 1, and models an honest 6.8-7.9% reply range without multiplying gains the pilot never tested together.
o1.biggest_mistake: Steps need a compliance footer and opt-out line (CAN-SPAM), and there's no follow-up play for the many 'later' or 'in audit' replies beyond a one-line note, which leaks value from a 6.8% reply pool.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the postal address and reply-stop opt-out to each email plus a concrete handoff for positive replies, without breaking the 120-word cap.

o2.biggest_strength: Sharp, honest targeting and a clean compliance footer, plus smart send-window timing around the close cycle.
o2.biggest_mistake: Several asks are two-in-one or misaligned (a 20-minute call asked in step 1 even though links were the loser, asking for a name, and no sign-off/name in the emails), and Step 2's opening line reads like a deflection rather than a finance peer easing a real fear.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Cut to one ask per email, strip the meeting-ask in step 1, sign each email with sender name and title, and write the finance-pain line into the first paragraph instead of the 'fair worry' framing.

reason: Output 1 reads like a finance person wrote it, keeps one ask per email, and stays disciplined on the data; Output 2 has good bones but its multi-ask emails and missing sign-offs make it less ready to send tomorrow.
